cohort: The study included 112 singleton pregnant women with intramural leiomyoma and 168 singleton pregnant women without leiomyoma (control group), whose hospital records were reviewed from 2009 to 2013.
finding: Pregnancy associated intramural leiomyoma (>= 3 cm) was found to be a significant risk factor for abortion, hospitalization for pain, premature rupture of membranes, oligohydramnios, preterm birth, breech and other abnormal presentations, and neonatal intensive care need.
mod_finding: No correlation was found between intramural leiomyoma and the rate of cesarean section.
followup_time: Immediate neonatal period (neonatal intensive care need mentioned as an outcome)
birth_weight: N/A (Intrauterine growth restriction was an outcome but no specific birth weight range for the cohort was mentioned)
gest_age: N/A (Preterm birth was an outcome but no specific gestational age range for the cohort was mentioned)
